Worn shock absorbers control wheel contact with the road less effectively; bouncing can cause uneven tread wear.
Engine oil lubricates engine parts, and too little can damage them. Stability depends instead on factors such as tire and suspension condition.
Load placement affects the center of gravity and stability. Keeping the load low and near the center line helps keep the vehicle stable.
Worn shock absorbers do not guarantee fuel savings: they control oscillations less effectively and can impair road holding.
Less damping does not improve comfort: it allows the body to continue oscillating and bouncing.

The quiz marks this FALSE, but an asphalt temperature of 25°C alone cannot diagnose instability. On warm roads winter tyres can make handling less precise, depending on the tyre and manoeuvre, so the sources consulted do not rule out the possibility described.
A navigation system gives route guidance but does not control the vehicle’s stance. Stability depends on factors such as tires and suspension.
Incorrect toe alignment makes the wheels run at the wrong angles and can wear the tread edges unevenly.
Excessive pressure makes the tire less able to absorb impacts, producing a harsher and less comfortable ride.
An underinflated tire deforms more sideways. More steering is needed for the same cornering force, and road holding can worsen.
Wheel imbalance can cause vibration, including at the steering wheel, and uneven tread wear.
When dual tires are underinflated, their sidewalls can deform until they touch. Rubbing wears them and can damage them.
Abnormal wear can indicate a pressure or alignment problem. Report it to the person responsible so it can be checked and corrected.
Excessive heat can indicate tire damage, including internal damage. Do not resume the trip; inform the company and have the tire checked.
Incorrect toe alignment can cause wear and impair steering precision; it does not reduce the risk of skidding.
Imbalance can cause vibration and uneven wear, but it is not a device that shortens braking distance.
Low pressure makes the tire flex and heat up; it is not a direct cause of increased engine coolant temperature.
Uneven wear calls for inspection of the tire and possible causes. It does not always require stopping on the spot and waiting for assistance: the defect’s severity matters.
Uneven wear and its cause must be checked. Immediate replacement with the spare is not automatically necessary; it depends on the tire’s condition.
Uneven wear should be reported and assessed. It does not automatically require immediately unloading goods or passengers and continuing empty.
The driver must be able to see the road and other road users. Obstructions in the field of view can hide hazards and delay reactions.
Stickers and objects on the windscreen can obstruct the field of vision: the driver must be able to see the road unobstructed.
Clean, working mirrors let the driver check what is happening behind and beside the vehicle.
Clean, transparent windows, including the side windows, allow an unobstructed view of the road and other road users.
Washer fluid lets the washer remove dirt from the windscreen and maintain good visibility.
Worn blades can leave areas uncleared. Checking and replacing them when needed keeps the wipers effective.
Tape does not repair damaged glass. The damage should be assessed and the windscreen repaired or replaced as appropriate, keeping the field of vision clear.
Opaque films can obstruct visibility: the windows must allow the driver to see adequately.
The inspection checks the condition of reflectors; it does not require all of them to be replaced at every inspection. Defective ones must be put right.
The inspection checks the headlights; it does not require bulbs to be changed at every inspection. A faulty light must be put right.
The inspection does not require every fuse to be replaced. A fuse protects a circuit and should be replaced if faulty after identifying the cause.
Regulated vehicle repair is reserved for authorised, registered businesses; the law excludes some simple operations, such as changing oil and air and oil filters.
Vehicle repair businesses are subject to registration and environmental rules. Even operations excluded from the definition of vehicle repair must comply with waste rules.
The rules for vehicle repair businesses aim to improve service qualifications and road safety, reducing the risk of poorly performed work.
The law expressly excludes changing the air filter from vehicle repair; waste rules still apply.
The law expressly excludes changing the oil filter from vehicle repair; the used filter must be handled under waste rules.
The law excludes changing oil and other lubricating fluids from vehicle repair, but requires compliance with environmental rules.
Changing engine coolant is expressly excluded from vehicle repair; used coolant must be handled properly.
Even when a change may be done personally, used fluids and filters must be handled in accordance with waste rules.
An ordinary public waste bin does not ensure proper handling of used fluids and filters. They must be taken to the collection service designated locally for such waste.
Leaving fluids beside bins amounts to abandoning waste. They must be handed over through the appropriate collection service.
A bag left beside bins is not proper disposal: used filters must be handled through the designated collection arrangements.
Replacing brake pads concerns a vehicle component and falls within vehicle repair; it is not among the replacements expressly excluded by law.
Replacing shock absorbers concerns vehicle components and falls within vehicle repair; it is not among the replacements expressly excluded by law.
Repairing the lighting system falls within vehicle repair: the law includes restoring vehicle components.
Repairing the electrical system falls within vehicle repair: the law includes restoring vehicle components.
Vehicle repair businesses must be authorized and listed in the business register or artisans’ register; a municipal list alone is not enough.

Repairs to the timing mechanism and fuel supply or injection systems belong to regulated vehicle repair and should be entrusted to an authorized business; replacing filters is distinct from those repairs.
Cold liquid added to a very hot engine can cause thermal shock and damage components. Let the system cool before opening or topping it up.
Gearbox repairs concern transmission components and fall under regulated vehicle repair: use an authorized business with a qualified technical manager.
For repairs covered by vehicle repair regulations, use an authorized business listed in the business register or artisans’ register.
Replacing air and oil filters is excluded from regulated vehicle repair and is not reserved for authorized workshops. Environmental and waste rules still apply.
A diploma alone does not authorize a driver to carry out major repairs: regulated repairs should be entrusted to an authorized business with a qualified technical manager.
A driving licence authorizes driving, not transmission repair. Entrust that repair to an authorized vehicle repair business.
Changing lubricating oil is excluded from regulated vehicle repair even for this truck; environmental and waste disposal rules still apply.
Change the oil at the manufacturer’s intervals: adequate lubrication helps protect the engine.
Checking the level at every refueling helps detect oil consumption before the level becomes too low. Follow the procedure in the vehicle manual.

The driver can carry out routine maintenance of the air and oil filters, including cleaning when prescribed for the type of filter. The law expressly excludes their replacement from regulated vehicle repair; follow the manual and waste disposal rules.
There is no general requirement to replace a cylinder head gasket every 20,000 km: repair it when necessary, following diagnosis and the manufacturer’s instructions.
Glow plugs help with cold starting: they do not need automatic replacement every 10,000 km. They are checked and replaced when needed, following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Coolant should be changed according to the manufacturer’s schedule; 25,000 km is not a universal interval.

The original or an authenticated copy of the latest payslip is one form of employment proof provided for in the 2005 decision for the covered case. The contract is another option in the specified form, with a current-employment declaration if it is more than six months old.

An indivisible beam whose dimensions cause the dimensional limits to be exceeded may result in exceptional transport: the case provided for under Article 10 also requires compliance with the applicable mass limits. The prescribed conditions and authorisations must be observed.

Transporting live animals in connection with an economic activity can require transporter authorization from the competent authority, through the ASL in Italy. The type and exceptions depend on the activity and journey.

For frozen and quick-frozen foodstuffs covered by ATP, certain brief operations, such as defrosting the evaporator, may permit a temporary rise of up to 3 °C above the applicable temperature on the surface of products in part of the load.
Heavy braking can shift the load or loosen restraints: stop somewhere safe and check its position and securing before continuing.

The black R on yellow identifies hazardous waste in the package, not hazardous goods generally. The requirement for transporting such waste calls for a permanent, legible label or mark on packages; dangerous goods rules may also apply.

The vehicle and tank must suit the goods under the applicable ADR requirements: the tank code identifies characteristics and permitted substances, and inspections are required. Certain vehicle categories require specific approval.
ATP is the international agreement on the carriage of perishable foodstuffs and the special equipment used for it.

Exceptional circulation generally requires authorization from the authority responsible for the route. Exceptions apply: for example, an exceptional vehicle may travel without it when it meets ordinary dimension and mass limits and the prescribed swept envelope.
The goods determine the cargo space and payload needed; the route may require a vehicle suited to size and access restrictions.
The semitrailer can be detached for loading or unloading, leaving the tractor available for other work.

The quiz marks VERO, but the rules have changed: ADR 2003 required the consignor to give instructions to the driver and information about their contents to the carrier; this is not the same wording as the question. Under ADR 2025 the carrier supplies the written instructions to the crew before the journey in languages they understand.
Liability for nonperformance or delay can be excluded if it is proved to result from a cause not attributable to the party concerned; delay alone does not establish this.

Place a heavy package near the vehicle’s centre line to support lateral stability. Its position along the bed must still be checked against permitted axle loads: the geometric centre alone does not guarantee correct distribution.
Smooth maneuvers limit forces that can shift goods; the load must still be secured against forces encountered on the road.
Perishable goods can deteriorate quickly: journey time and storage conditions, such as temperature, affect their quality.
Sand can scatter during a journey. A properly secured sheet contains it and helps prevent it falling onto the road.
The goods must be within the available payload, and their size must fit the cargo space and dimensional limits.
Delay means performance beyond the agreed deadline; it is distinct from loss of or damage to the goods.
The driver promptly reports the obstacle to the company for instructions. The carrier must immediately ask the sender for instructions and safeguard the goods.
Total loss concerns all the goods entrusted and not delivered; the cause of nondelivery is separate from the question of the carrier’s liability.
Loss is partial when only part of the quantity entrusted arrives: for example, packages or part of the weight may be missing.
Delivery gives effect to the transport contract: the place, deadline and manner are those agreed or, failing that, those established by custom.
Damage means deterioration of the delivered goods: the quantity may arrive, but its condition has worsened and its value fallen.
The tachograph card identifies the driver and records activities; it does not prove employment by a particular company.
Overloading incurs the penalties applicable to the measured mass and excess; the stated excess does not automatically lead to licence suspension.
A suitable vehicle is not enough: for transport covered by the regulation, the applicable authorizations and training or certificates are also needed.
The goods are not automatically returned to the sender. The driver informs the company; the carrier must promptly ask the sender for instructions and safeguard the goods.
An absent consignee or refusal does not by itself require a police call. The driver informs the company; the carrier promptly asks the sender for instructions.

The quiz marks FALSO: ATP 2024 states up to 3 °C, not 1 °C, as the maximum permitted temporary rise on the surface of part of the load during certain brief operations. A 1 °C rise is nevertheless within the 3 °C limit when all conditions apply.
Under the registration conditions applicable to category 5, packages of hazardous waste carry a black R on yellow, not red RP on white. Applicable ADR requirements must also be followed.
ATP concerns perishable foodstuffs and special transport equipment. Dangerous goods are subject to the relevant ADR requirements, including those for the mode of carriage.

The quiz marks FALSO: the presence of dangerous goods alone does not specify which tyres to choose. Follow the vehicle and tyre specifications, including load and speed ratings, and the requirements applicable to the transport.
ATP denotes the agreement on international carriage of perishable foodstuffs and the special equipment used, not an authorization for petroleum products.
ATP concerns international carriage of perishable foodstuffs and the special equipment used; ADR covers dangerous goods by road.
Damage means harm or deterioration to the goods. Non-delivery can be delay or loss; under the CMR, loss may be presumed only under its conditions and after the specified periods.
When required, authorization for exceptional circulation is issued by the authorities responsible for the roads concerned, not by the provincial motor vehicle office.
The carrier provides ADR written instructions to the vehicle crew before departure, not the consignee to the carrier.

The absence of a fuel station on the route alone does not prove that delay or non-performance was due to a cause beyond the responsible party’s control: the possibility of arranging fuel also matters.
A heavy package overhanging the rear can alter axle loads. Its position must be chosen according to the permitted distribution for the vehicle and individual axle limits.
A fixed distance from the cab does not guarantee correct distribution: placement depends on the vehicle, package weight and axle limits.
A retarder does not replace securing: the load must be blocked or lashed to withstand forces during braking and cornering.

Sand must be arranged to prevent dispersal. Wetting it is not required if dispersal is prevented another way, for example with a suitable cover.
Sand must be contained to prevent dispersal, but a closed body is not the only permitted means: a suitable cover can also be used.
Payload alone is insufficient: axle limits must also be respected and the load appropriately arranged and secured.
Available volume alone is insufficient: permitted masses and axle limits must also be respected and the load secured.

If the consignee cannot be found, refuses or delays delivery, the carrier must immediately ask the consignor for instructions. Storage is available only under the legal conditions, not automatically at the nearest warehouse.
Delay concerns delivery after the applicable deadline; a breakdown can cause it but is not its definition.
A reduction in the quantity delivered is partial loss; delay concerns the time of delivery.
Deterioration reducing the value of goods is damage. Total loss instead concerns failure to deliver all the goods.

The quiz marks FALSO, but the wording does not say the whole shipment is missing: failure to deliver part can also constitute partial loss. Loss concerns missing goods; damage concerns deterioration. Non-delivery can also be a delay.
Goods must be made available at the place, time and in the manner specified by the contract or custom; public storage is not the mandatory ordinary destination.
Missing the delivery deadline is delay; damage is instead harm to the goods.

The driver checks that the documents required for the cargo are available on board and reports any missing documents before departure. Preparing and supplying documents belong to the responsible parties; the driver does not necessarily create them all.
Smooth driving limits forces that can damage goods; the carrier must preserve them until delivery.
Lashings can loosen during the journey: if necessary, stop and restore them so that the load remains secured.

Before accepting the load, the driver checks accessible packages for obvious leaks and reports problems to the loader or carrier: a leaking package must not be loaded. The ADR assigns distinct checks to the loader and carrier.
Knowing the load and instructions allows appropriate precautions, for example for hazardous or sensitive goods.
Drivers must obey speed limits: they are responsible for speeding, although others may also be liable depending on the circumstances.
A driver who operates an overloaded vehicle can be penalized; the rules also provide for liability of other parties.
The driver must observe the applicable driving and rest periods; the undertaking also has duties in organizing work and may be liable for infringements.

Being after 7 p.m. alone does not give a general right to refuse delivery: the agreement, instructions and actual receiving conditions matter.
